label: sets directly

label: dual mandate signal

label: anchors short end
notes: 2Y yield tightly tracks fed funds rate expectations

label: rate differential

notes: Tech is long-duration. Higher rates compress DCF valuations more than other sectors.

notes: Banks earn more on loans vs deposits when rates rise. NIM expands.

notes: VIX spikes coincide with equity selloffs. Not purely causal — both reflect risk-off.

label: credit stress signal
notes: Widening HY spreads often lead equity weakness by a few days

label: fiscal stimulus
notes: Deficit spending adds to aggregate demand. Multiplier effect varies by type.

label: rate differential
notes: ECB easing weakens EUR vs USD when Fed holds. Divergence is the key driver.

label: carry trade driver
notes: Higher US rates widen US-Japan rate differential, attracting carry traders long USD/JPY.

label: growth drives hiring
notes: Okun's Law: ~2% GDP growth needed to hold unemployment stable

label: spending intention
notes: Consumer spending is ~70% of US GDP. Sentiment is a leading indicator.

label: credit conditions
notes: Rate hikes tighten credit conditions, widening HY spreads over time

notes: Rising long-end yields compress tech valuations via DCF discount rate

label: wealth effect
notes: Rising equity prices boost household net worth and spending confidence

notes: Rate hikes push up long-end yields, though effect is weaker than on 2Y

label: safe-haven flight to gold
notes: Gold hit record highs above $2,400 as investors sought safe-haven assets amid escalation fears

label: safe-haven demand strengthens USD
notes: Dollar strengthened on safe-haven flows; consistent with flight-to-safety dynamics in prior geopolitical shocks

label: risk-off selloff on escalation fears
notes: US equities fell on initial news but recovered as limited retaliation scope became clear; net impact muted

label: geopolitical shock spikes implied vol
notes: Uncertainty around escalation path and potential oil supply disruption drove near-term volatility premium

label: flight-to-safety bid on Treasuries
notes: Yields initially dropped on flight-to-safety Treasury buying before rebounding as risk sentiment stabilised

label: short-end safety bid
notes: Front end also caught safe-haven bid; rebound was faster as geopolitical risk was contained within days

label: higher-for-longer lifts real yields
notes: Hawkish Fed signalling pushes nominal yields up; if inflation expectations are anchored, real yields rise in tandem

label: rising real yields pressure BTC
notes: Higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding speculative assets; well-documented in 2022 cycle

label: rising real yields pressure gold
notes: Gold is a non-yielding asset; real yield is its primary macro driver. Article notes gold initially sold off before recovering on safe-haven demand

label: nominal yield component of real yield
notes: Real yield = nominal 10Y minus breakeven inflation; nominal move is the primary driver when inflation expectations are stable

label: BTC leads ETH directionally
notes: Ethereum moves directionally with Bitcoin with higher beta; near-simultaneous in this event

label: crypto price decline hits exchange equity
notes: Coinbase revenues tied to trading volumes and asset prices; equity trades as a leveraged proxy for crypto market sentiment

label: price decline slows ETF inflows
notes: Retail and institutional appetite for crypto ETF exposure cools when spot prices fall sharply

label: higher real yields reduce risk appetite for crypto ETFs
notes: Rising real yields shift capital allocation away from speculative high-beta assets including crypto ETF products

label: crypto-tech risk-off correlation
notes: Analysts note crypto increasingly correlates with Nasdaq/tech; shared macro driver of real yields and risk appetite means co-movement in risk-off episodes

label: rising vol triggers crypto de-risking
notes: Bitcoin behaves as high-beta risk asset; VIX spikes associated with leveraged position unwinds in crypto

notes: Executive sanctions on oil producers (Iran, Russia, Venezuela) restrict supply and raise prices

label: safe haven demand
notes: Geopolitical escalation drives safe haven USD demand

label: policy uncertainty
notes: Trade wars, sanctions, and policy uncertainty weigh on equity risk premium

notes: Semiconductor export controls and China tech restrictions hit tech sector directly

notes: OPEC production cuts raise oil prices which pass through to headline CPI with ~6 week lag

label: revenue uplift
notes: Production cuts raise oil prices benefiting energy sector earnings

label: deficit supply pressure
notes: Large deficit spending increases Treasury supply, pushing up long-end yields

label: demand stimulus
notes: Fiscal stimulus adds to aggregate demand, contributing to inflation with a lag

label: transfer payments
notes: Direct stimulus payments and unemployment benefits support consumer confidence

label: budget proposals
notes: Executive budget proposals shape congressional spending priorities

label: credit tightening
notes: Wide HY spreads signal tight credit conditions that slow business investment and GDP

label: hiring freeze
notes: Credit stress leads companies to freeze hiring and cut headcount

label: NIM expansion
notes: Steeper yield curve expands bank net interest margins, boosting financials

label: mortgage demand
notes: Strong housing market drives mortgage origination and fee income for banks

label: wealth effect
notes: Rising home values increase household net worth and consumer confidence

label: earnings headwind
notes: Strong USD hurts S&P 500 multinationals by reducing overseas earnings in dollar terms

label: framework deal announcement de-escalates conflict
notes: Trump announced a framework agreement and called off a planned round of US strikes, the most concrete de-escalation step in the months-long war; primary driver of the two-session oil selloff

label: Tehran pushback sustains residual risk premium
notes: Iranian state-affiliated outlet Fars denied Tehran had approved any draft memorandum, undercutting Trump's framework claim; tempers the de-escalation but did not reverse Friday's continued price decline

label: conflict intensity drives Hormuz disruption level
notes: Throughout the 2026 war, escalation phases coincided with naval blockades and dark-fleet activity through Hormuz; this de-escalation event corresponds to easing disruption, with reopening explicitly conditioned on deal finalization

label: Hormuz disruption severity sets oil supply-risk premium
notes: ~20% of global crude flows transit Hormuz; closure/blockade phases drove WTI/Brent to $115+/$140, and easing disruption expectations drove the fall to ~$86 here. JPMorgan estimated ~2mbpd still moving via dark fleet during blockade, implying any reopening is only partial near-term

label: Israeli strikes on Iran complicate US-brokered de-escalation
notes: Israel struck central/western Iran (Isfahan, Tabriz, Tehran) days before this deal announcement, despite Trump's calls for restraint; illustrates the fragile, non-linear path toward the framework agreement and a recurring risk of relapse

label: US pressures Israel to avoid retaliation during talks
notes: Reports indicate Trump called the Israeli PM to advise against retaliation; speculative as a market-relevant causal lever but relevant to the stability of any ceasefire/deal

label: falling oil lowers inflation breakevens, pulling yields down
notes: Bloomberg reported bond yields 'sinking' alongside oil's slide to ~$86, even as risk-on sentiment would normally unwind safe-haven Treasury demand (which alone implies higher yields). The dominant effect here was the inflation-expectations/breakeven channel, distinct from the flight-to-safety edge already in the graph

label: falling oil lowers near-term inflation expectations
notes: Front-end yields are highly sensitive to near-term inflation/Fed-path expectations; falling energy prices reduce the urgency of further Fed tightening

label: lower gas/freight costs lift consumer confidence
notes: Article explicitly ties Victoria's Secret's rally to 'improved consumer confidence and lower freight costs' following the oil price decline; a well-known but previously uncaptured pass-through from energy prices to sentiment

label: lower long rates support REIT valuations
notes: Standard rate-sensitivity mechanism via cap rates and financing costs - a well-established edge missing from the graph. Note: real estate actually declined today despite falling yields, reflecting a rotation effect (capital moving into cyclicals/tech on the risk-on day) that this edge alone doesn't capture - flagged for review

label: lower long rates support utilities as bond-proxies
notes: Utilities trade as bond-proxy/dividend plays, well-established inverse rate sensitivity. As with real estate, today's decline reflects a defensive-sector rotation effect competing with this mechanism

label: falling vol disproportionately lifts high-beta tech
notes: Tech/growth has higher market beta than the broad index; VIX fell ~12% while tech (and the chipmaker gauge, +8%) led gains, consistent with high-beta names outperforming on sharp de-risking days

label: draft deal commits US to lift oil sanctions on Iran
notes: OFAC/Treasury sanctions designations are a direct US executive policy lever; the reported 14-point MOU explicitly includes 'lifting of oil sanctions' as a term, distinct from and additional to the Hormuz transit provisions

label: sanctions relief implies incremental Iranian supply, pressuring prices
notes: A distinct supply-side channel from strait_of_hormuz_status: Hormuz reopening restores transit for ALL Gulf producers, whereas sanctions relief specifically unlocks Iran's own suppressed export capacity (~1.5-2.5mbpd historically under sanctions vs ~3.5-4mbpd potential). Markets reprice on the announcement immediately (lag 0), though physical export ramp-up historically takes 6-12 months (cf. 2015-16 JCPOA relief)
